Use **`FunctionAgent`** from LlamaIndex's prebuilt agent workflows. The docs describe it as one of the "pre-built agentic workflows like `FunctionAgent`" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/understanding/agent/index.md]. The agents guide shows the import as "from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import FunctionAgent" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md].

Pass your tools as plain Python functions in the `tools` list, with an LLM and a system prompt:

```python
from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import FunctionAgent
from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI

def multiply(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Useful for multiplying two numbers."""
    return a * b

agent = FunctionAgent(
    tools=[multiply],
    llm=OpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini"),
    system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant that can multiply two numbers.",
)
```

This example is from the agents guide [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/index.md]. The snippet is cut off after the system prompt, so the retrieved text doesn't show how to run the agent.

Write a clear docstring for each tool. The tool name and description guide which tool the LLM picks and what arguments it writes: "the tool selected (and the arguments written for that tool) rely strongly on the **tool name** and **description** of the tools purpose and arguments" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/deploying/agents/tools.md].

If you need more control than a prebuilt agent gives you, the docs point to building custom agentic workflows with LlamaIndex Workflows, and to a "Building a ReAct agent workflow" example [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/use_cases/agents.md].

I can't confirm from these excerpts whether `FunctionAgent` is the newest or preferred option for every version, so check the current API reference if you're on a recent release.
